title: Augmented strict adic reduction under ringed open extension
statement:
Let $e:W\hookrightarrow T$ be an open immersion of schemes [def-weil-open-immersion] and let $A,I,P_n=A/I^n,A_T,A_W$ be the completed coefficient datum of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], with $n\ge1$. Identify $A_T|_W=A_W$ and $(P_n)_T|_W=(P_n)_W$ by [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization]. Let $e_!$ mean sheafification of the extension presheaf [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf, def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], on modules, complexes and strict towers. For every $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_W))$ there is a canonical natural isomorphism in $D(\operatorname{Tow}_A(T))$
$$\rho_{e,K}:(e_!K)_\bullet\xrightarrow{\sim}e_!(K_\bullet).$$
For a flat-term K-flat representative $P$ of $K$, it is represented by the actual strict complex map whose $n$-th component is
$$(e_!P)\otimes_{A_T}(P_n)_T\longrightarrow e_!\bigl(P\otimes_{A_W}(P_n)_W\bigr),\quad [p]\otimes b\longmapsto[p\otimes b|_W].$$
Brackets denote the extension-presheaf summand indexed by a map to $W$, followed by sheafification. The map is independent of the representative after localization. It commutes with every quotient transition, and with the quotient augmentations $\Delta(e_!P)\to(e_!P\otimes(P_n)_T)_n$ and $e_!\Delta P\to e_!(P\otimes(P_n)_W)_n$, both $p\mapsto p\otimes1$. At level $n$ it also identifies reduction as $(P_n)_T$-modules, before restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. For $b\ge a\ge1$ it respects the quotient normalization $(K_b\otimes^L_{(P_b)_W}(P_a)_W)\cong K_a$, including the equal-index unit and three-index cocycle of the datum. No completeness of $K$ or quasi-compactness of $e$ is required.

source.place: Tensor/reduction argument, including scalar restriction and quotient augmentations; Stacks 0GL1, sites-cohomology.tex, lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor; strict normalization is an agent-written refinement.

proof.text: Put $R=A_T$, $S_n=(P_n)_T$, and write $J=e_!$. The slice equivalence $W_{\mathrm{proet}}\simeq T_{\mathrm{proet}}/W$ is [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] (1), and restriction is $F|_W(V)=F(V\to T)$ by its part (3). By [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], $(P_n)_T$ is the ring sheafification of the presheaf $C_{n,T}:U\mapsto\operatorname{Cont}(\pi_0(|U|),P_n)$; since $C_{n,T}(V\to T)$ depends only on the scheme $V$, the restricted presheaf $C_{n,T}|_W$ is $C_{n,W}$ under this equivalence. The natural isomorphism $(C_{n,T}|_W)^\#\cong(C_{n,T}^\#)|_W$ of [lem-pur-ring-presheaf-sheafification-localization] gives $S_n|_W=(P_n)_W$; its naturality in the presheaf, applied to the postcomposition maps $C_{b,T}\to C_{a,T}$, shows that it carries $q_{b,a}|_W$ to $q_{b,a}$. Restriction is sectionwise and $A_T$ is the sectionwise limit of compatible families, so $R|_W=\varprojlim_n S_n|_W=A_W$ with the same projections. Thus these are the same localized ringed sites with all their ring maps, not discrete constant $A$-coefficient categories. By [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], $J$ is exact. Choose a termwise surjective flat-term K-flat resolution $P\to C$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. By [lem-cbc-ringed-open-flat-resolution], $JP\to JC$ is again such a resolution. Applying exact $J$ levelwise is exact on towers, since kernels and cokernels are levelwise [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]; its termwise derived functor is therefore available by [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. Consequently both sides of the desired comparison can be computed from this single $P$.

proof.text: For a flat $R|_W$-module $G$ and an $R$-module $B$, use the ringed slice tensor formula [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-extension-tensor]. Fix its canonical direction $JG\otimes_R B\to J(G\otimes_{R|_W}B|_W)$ as follows. The inverse is the $J\dashv e^*$-adjunct of the open unit tensored with identity, exactly the normalization of $\gamma^{-1}$ in [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization]. Because $G$ and $JG$ are flat by Step 1, tensor with either is exact, so each, concentrated in degree zero, is K-flat and these derived tensors are the ordinary tensors. On the extension summand over $V\to W$, this inverse sends $[g\otimes b]$ to $[g]\otimes b$: the unit sends $g$ to that same section on the open. The forward map is therefore $[g]\otimes b\mapsto[g\otimes b|_W]$. These formulas respect $(rg)\otimes b=g\otimes rb$, addition and restrictions. The two composites are identities on the displayed tensors and hence on the sheaf morphisms by the tensor and module-sheafification universal properties [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], with extension summands as in [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf]. Apply this with $G=P^q$ and $B=S_n$. Naturality in $G$ makes it commute with $d_P^q$, so these maps give actual chain isomorphisms $\delta_{P,n}:JP\otimes_R S_n\to J(P\otimes_{R|_W}S_n|_W)$.

source.place: Tag 0GL1 (lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor), using sites-modules.tex Tag 0E8I; strict quotient/augmentation refinement written out here.

proof.text: For any $b\ge a$, the two composites in the transition square for $\delta_P$ send $[p]\otimes r$ to $[p\otimes q_{b,a}(r)|_W]$. Thus the $\delta_{P,n}$ and their inverses form inverse maps of actual strict tower complexes, with the specified quotient transitions of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. For $s\in S_n$ the equality $\delta_{P,n}([p]\otimes rs)=[p\otimes r|_Ws|_W]=s\delta_{P,n}([p]\otimes r)$ proves $S_n$-linearity. Applying extension using $S_n$ as coefficient ring or extending the same sheaf after restriction to $R$ gives the same underlying abelian sheafification; its action is uniquely extended from the same presheaf action [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. Hence this is already a comparison of $S_n$-module complexes, and only afterwards of $R$-module complexes by [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars].

proof.text: Termwise extension of the constant tower on $P$ is the constant tower on $JP$, with identity transitions. At every index, $\delta_{P,n}$ sends the quotient augmentation $[p]\mapsto[p]\otimes1$ to $[p\otimes1]$, which is exactly $J$ applied to the augmentation of $P$. The augmentations are strict maps because $q_{b,a}(1)=1$. The equality on extension summands extends uniquely through module sheafification [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf, def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], so this is an equality of augmented strict complex diagrams before localization, not just equality of evaluated derived arrows.

source.place: Tag 0GL1 (lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor), using sites-modules.tex Tag 0E8I; strict quotient/augmentation refinement written out here.

proof.text: For $b\ge a$, the coefficient complex $Q_b=P\otimes_{A_W}(P_b)_W$ is K-flat with flat terms over $(P_b)_W$ by [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings]. Apply [lem-cbc-ringed-open-flat-resolution] again with coefficient ring $(P_b)_T$: $JQ_b$ is K-flat over that ring. Thus both successive reductions in the normalization square are computed by ordinary tensor complexes. The normalization of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] sends $(p\otimes r)\otimes s$ to $p\otimes q_{b,a}(r)s$. Starting with $([p]\otimes r)\otimes s$, the path using $\delta_{P,b}$, then the comparison of Step 2 over the ring $(P_b)_T$ with $G=Q_b^q$ (flat over $(P_b)_W$) and $B=(P_a)_T$, and then $J$ of normalization gives $[p\otimes q_{b,a}(r)|_Ws|_W]$. Normalizing first on $T$ and then using $\delta_{P,a}$ gives the identical expression. Tensor and sheafification uniqueness give equality of the chain maps. When $b=a$ this is the tensor unit $(p\otimes r)\otimes s\mapsto p\otimes rs$. For $c\ge b\ge a$, both composites give $[p\otimes q_{c,a}(r)|_Wq_{b,a}(s)|_Wt|_W]$ on $(([p]\otimes r)\otimes s)\otimes t$. This proves compatibility with the equal-index unit and three-index cocycle, with the quotient coefficient actions retained.

source.place: Tag 0GL1 (lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor), using sites-modules.tex Tag 0E8I; strict quotient/augmentation refinement written out here.

proof.text: For every chain map $f:P\to P'$ between flat-term K-flat complexes, both naturality-square paths send $[p]\otimes r$ to $[f(p)\otimes r|_W]$. Thus $\delta_P$ is a natural chain isomorphism on this class and induces one on its homotopy category. If $f$ is a quasi-isomorphism, $Jf$ is one by exactness, and $JP,JP'$ are K-flat by Step 1. By [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], tensoring either $f$ or $Jf$ with each quotient gives a quasi-isomorphism; the tower maps are quasi-isomorphisms by levelwise cohomology [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. The first assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] identifies the localization of the flat-term K-flat homotopy category with $D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_W))$. The localization universal property [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] therefore descends $\delta$ and its inverse to a natural isomorphism $\rho_{e,K}$. On a representative $P$ its endpoints are precisely the two reduction constructions of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], since $JP$ is K-flat. This also proves independence of all representatives: comparison along any inverted quasi-isomorphism is forced by the naturality square, and these comparisons compose. The strict augmentation equality of Step 4 and the coefficient/normalization equalities of Steps 3 and 5 remain equalities under localization. No step used completeness of $K$ or quasi-compactness of $e$.
